name: Oxybutynin for sweating
lead: Oxybutynin is an anticholinergic (antimuscarinic) medication approved in the US in 1975 for overactive bladder. It is also used off-label to reduce excessive sweating, increasingly since the 2010s [1].

Wikipedia notes that, as of 2024, this use remains off-label because dosing and the full side-effect profile are not established [1]. Reference sources list oral anticholinergics such as oxybutynin among treatments for focal and generalized hyperhidrosis, with side effects including dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation and vision changes [2].
Published studies include a double-blind placebo-controlled trial in depressed patients on sertraline, and several registered studies in hyperhidrosis [3][4][5].
infobox: Oral (also transdermal, gel for bladder uses)

paras: Oxybutynin blocks acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors. It is metabolised in the liver into N-desethyloxybutynin, an active metabolite thought to contribute much of its side effects [1].

A double-blind, placebo-controlled study of 140 depressed patients treated with sertraline examined oxybutynin for the sweating that is a common effect of SSRIs; the abstract reports that oxybutynin reduces sweating [3]. Registered studies include a long-term study of 1,100 participants (started 2007) [4] and a phase 2 comparison with placebo in women with plantar hyperhidrosis (32 participants) [5]. Results of these registrations are not summarised in the available record.

Common effects include dry mouth, constipation, dizziness and sleep problems; serious risks include urinary retention, heat stroke because reduced sweating impairs cooling, and delirium [1]. A large study linked cumulative anticholinergic use to dementia risk in people over 65 [1]. Contraindications include untreated narrow-angle glaucoma and gastrointestinal obstruction [1].

timeline.event: Oxybutynin approved for medical use in the US [1].

card.summary: A bladder drug used off-label as a sweat blocker, with a placebo-controlled trial behind it and a full anticholinergic side-effect profile.
card.note: Off-label for sweating; anticholinergic side effects include heat stroke risk.

quick.overview:
Oxybutynin is a prescription anticholinergic drug approved for overactive bladder and prescribed off-label for excessive sweating. A 2012 double-blind trial reported reduced sweating in sertraline-treated patients.

As of 2024 its use for sweating remains off-label.
quick.mechanism: It blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors, reducing the signal that activates sweat glands.
quick.risks: Dry mouth, constipation, dizziness, urinary retention, heat stroke and delirium are listed; a large study linked cumulative anticholinergic use to dementia risk in people over 65.
